questions.q: Which saying of the Prophet opens the editorial’s note of thanks?
options: “Thanks are due to God alone”
Not quite. The article says: “One who does not thank the people, does not thank God”.
“Thank people only for great favours”
Not quite. The article says: “One who does not thank the people, does not thank God”.
“One who is thanked should give thanks twice”
Not quite. The article says: “One who does not thank the people, does not thank God”.
“One who does not thank the people, does not thank God”
Yes. Gratitude to God includes acknowledging those who help us.
questions.rationale: “The Prophet Muhammad said, ‘One who does not thank the people, does not thank God.’”

questions.q: When the Maulana first thought of starting a magazine, a friend tried to dissuade him. On what ground?
options: He was too young to edit one
Not quite. The article says: Nobody reads reflective magazines; people prefer informative writing.
There was no money for printing
Not quite. The article says: Nobody reads reflective magazines; people prefer informative writing.
There were too many magazines already
Not quite. The article says: Nobody reads reflective magazines; people prefer informative writing.
Nobody reads reflective magazines; people prefer informative writing
Right. Its decades of publication answer the doubt.
questions.rationale: “He was dissuaded by saying that nobody reads suggestive magazines and that people preferred informative writings.”

questions.q: One of the stated objectives of the magazine concerns duties and rights. What is it?
options: To help people secure their rights
Not quite. The article says: To help people become duty-conscious instead of right-conscious.
To free people from duties
Not quite. The article says: To help people become duty-conscious instead of right-conscious.
To teach people the law
Not quite. The article says: To help people become duty-conscious instead of right-conscious.
To help people become duty-conscious instead of right-conscious
Well read. Asking first what one owes.
questions.rationale: “To help people become duty-conscious instead of becoming right-conscious.”

questions.q: The article traces three views of the universe’s basic building block. In what order did they come?
options: Matter, then consciousness, then energy
Not quite. The article says: Matter, then energy, then consciousness.
Matter, then energy, then consciousness
Correct. Science moved from the material towards the immaterial.
Consciousness, then matter, then energy
Not quite. The article says: Matter, then energy, then consciousness.
Energy, then matter, then consciousness
Not quite. The article says: Matter, then energy, then consciousness.
questions.rationale: “First, we had the Newtonian hypothesis that matter was the basic building block… this gave way to the Einsteinian paradigm of energy… And the latest is… consciousness.”

questions.article: Alarm for the End of Human History
questions.q: Which attitude to the world’s resources does the article draw from the Quran?
options: Use them as gifts of God, without exceeding the bounds – neither extravagant nor niggardly
Yes. We are answerable for how we use them.
Store them for one’s own family
Not quite. The article says: Use them as gifts of God, without exceeding the bounds – neither extravagant nor niggardly.
Avoid using them at all
Not quite. The article says: Use them as gifts of God, without exceeding the bounds – neither extravagant nor niggardly.
Use as much as one can afford
Not quite. The article says: Use them as gifts of God, without exceeding the bounds – neither extravagant nor niggardly.
questions.rationale: “Eat and drink but exceed not the bounds: God does not love those who exceed the bounds. (7: 31)”

questions.q: An engineer found that his flood gates – and the whole of Mexico City – were sinking. What was the main cause?
options: Rising sea levels
Not quite. The article says: Too much water had been drawn from the layer beneath the city.
The weight of new buildings
Not quite. The article says: Too much water had been drawn from the layer beneath the city.
Too much water had been drawn from the layer beneath the city
Right. Man cannot use nature without respecting it.
Repeated earthquakes
Not quite. The article says: Too much water had been drawn from the layer beneath the city.
questions.rationale: “The main reason for the sinking is a hitherto unsuspected factor: the over-exploitation of the water layer of Mexico City’s subsoil.”

questions.q: The master asked each pupil what he saw before shooting at the clay bird. Why did only Arjuna pass?
options: He had the strongest bow
Not quite. The article says: He saw nothing but the bird’s eye – his whole attention was on the target.
He saw nothing but the bird’s eye – his whole attention was on the target
Well reasoned. The others saw trees, leaves and branches.
He described the whole tree most accurately
Not quite. The article says: He saw nothing but the bird’s eye – his whole attention was on the target.
He shot before the others were ready
Not quite. The article says: He saw nothing but the bird’s eye – his whole attention was on the target.
questions.rationale: “In order to achieve your goal, all your attention should be concentrated on the goal.”

questions.q: One reader, who had not completed even primary schooling, writes of how his thinking changed. How does he put it?
options: He thinks of “they” before “we”
Not quite. The article says: He no longer thinks in terms of “we and they,” but of “we and we”.
He now thinks only of himself
Not quite. The article says: He no longer thinks in terms of “we and they,” but of “we and we”.
He no longer thinks in terms of “we and they,” but of “we and we”
Well read. From community-based to universal thinking.
He has stopped thinking about others
Not quite. The article says: He no longer thinks in terms of “we and they,” but of “we and we”.
questions.rationale: “I no longer think in terms of ‘we and they’. I think now in terms of ‘we and we’.”

questions.q: For two thousand years astronomers assumed that the planets move in circles, until Kepler showed otherwise. What does the article call the greatest obstacle to progress?
options: The shortness of human life
Not quite. The article says: The mind that remains obstinately closed.
The distance of the stars
Not quite. The article says: The mind that remains obstinately closed.
The lack of instruments
Not quite. The article says: The mind that remains obstinately closed.
The mind that remains obstinately closed
Exactly. Unquestioned reverence shuts off other possibilities.
questions.rationale: “It must be conceded that the greatest obstacle to all progress is the mind that remains obstinately closed.”

questions.q: You run for shelter in heavy rain and for open ground in an earthquake. What does the article say this shows about patience and avoidance?
options: They are signs of a defeatist mind
Not quite. The article says: They are realism, not cowardice – the way to continue life’s journey.
They are needed only by the weak
Not quite. The article says: They are realism, not cowardice – the way to continue life’s journey.
They are realism, not cowardice – the way to continue life’s journey
Yes. And they are everyone’s duty, not only other people’s.
They are useful only against nature
Not quite. The article says: They are realism, not cowardice – the way to continue life’s journey.
questions.rationale: “Patience and avoidance are not signs of cowardice or a defeatist mentality. They are simply realistic approaches.”
